title: FactorIA keyframed 2D clip (*.anim.json)
description: A clip of keyframed tracks the Animator plays when it has no glTF model: Animator.clips maps a clip name to this file. Each track drives one field of one entity under the entity that plays the clip (the entity itself or a child found by names). Numbers, vectors, colours and angles interpolate between keys; bools, ints, enums, assets and rects only step. Errors name the file and the JSON pointer; docs/ANIMATION.md, "2D clips", explains the format and the Animator side.

doc.description: What the clip shows and when it is used.

duration.description: Length of the clip in seconds. No key or event is later than this. A looping clip wraps here.

loop.description: true repeats the clip, false stops on its last pose and sends "anim.finished". An Animator state's own `loop` overrides it.

tracks.description: The animated fields. Two tracks may not drive the same field channel.

events.description: Game events sent when the clip's time passes `t` (once per loop). They reach world.on(name, fn) and entity.animator.on(name, fn) with {id, clip, time} plus `data`.

path.description: Names (EntityInfo `name`) of the entities from the one that plays the clip down to the one to animate, joined with '/': "body/arm_l/hand". "" (the default) is the entity itself.

component.description: Reflected component name on that entity: "Transform", "Sprite"...

field.description: Reflected field of the component, optionally with one channel: "rotation.z", "position", "color.a", "flipX". Channels are x y z w, or r g b a for a Color.

keys.description: Keys in ascending order of `t`, one per time.

t.description: Seconds from the start of the clip, at most the clip's `duration`.

value.description: The value at `t`, shaped like the field: a number, an array of 2 to 4 numbers for a vector or colour, a bool, an integer, an enum name, an asset path or a rect. Before the first key and after the last the track holds that key's value.

interp.description: How the value reaches the next key. "linear" (default), "step" (holds until the next key), "bezier" (cubic Hermite curve using this key's `out` and the next key's `in`), or an easing name of tween(). Ignored by fields that only step.

in.description: bezier: slope arriving at this key, in field units per second; a number or an array shaped like the value. Missing tangents are made smooth from the neighbouring keys.

out.description: bezier: slope leaving this key, in field units per second; a number or an array shaped like the value.

t.description: Seconds from the start of the clip, at most the clip's `duration`.

data.description: Extra fields sent with the event. The keys id, clip and time are the engine's and cannot be used.
